title: Hide order storage behind a repository

task.text: The domain should ask for orders as if they lived in a collection.
`OrderRepository` is the port, already written. Implement it in memory and use it from a service.

items: `InMemoryOrderRepository` implements `OrderRepository`. `save` inserts or replaces by id; `findById` returns an empty `Optional` for unknown ids; `remove` ignores unknown ids.
`findByCustomer` returns that customer's orders sorted by `id().value()`, as a snapshot that later saves do not change.
`LoyaltyService(OrderRepository)` gives `points(customer)`: the sum of `totalCents() / 100` over that customer's orders. It must know only the port.

checks.title: A saved order can be found by id
Unknown ids and customers give empty results
Saving an existing id replaces it
Orders for a customer come back sorted by id
Remove deletes, and tolerates unknown ids
Returned lists do not change later
Points add up over the in-memory store
The in-memory store implements the port

hints.text: A repository is a collection-shaped seam. The service should see only the interface, and the storage detail should live in exactly one class behind it.

Keep a `Map<OrderId, Order>` inside `InMemoryOrderRepository`. `LoyaltyService` keeps a private final `OrderRepository` from its constructor. Filter and sort when you answer `findByCustomer`, so the result is a new list.
